## Purpose and Scope

This Reference Architecture Document illustrates how the Data Classification, Data Loss Prevention, and Data Masking and Tokenization ABBs compose into a governance architecture for sensitive data across cloud, application, and non-production environments.

**Paired ABBs**:
- [GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASSIFY-2.5.02 — Data Classification and Cataloging ABB](../GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASSIFY-2.5.02.md)
- [GUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05 — Data Loss Prevention ABB](../GUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05.md)
- [GUID-SEC-DATA-MASK-2.5.06 — Data Masking and Tokenization ABB](../GUID-SEC-DATA-MASK-2.5.06.md)

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#classification-driven-protection-flow]

### Classification-Driven Protection Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Ingestion["Data Ingestion"]
        SRC[Data Source\nDatabase, API, File, Stream]
    end

    subgraph Classification["Classification Layer"]
        AUTO[Automated Classification\nContent inspection and metadata detection]
        LABEL[Label Application\nSensitivity tier + regulatory sub-tier]
        CAT[Data Asset Catalog\nAsset registry with classification metadata]
    end

    subgraph Protection["Protection Routing"]
        ROUTE{Classification Tier?}
        ENC[Encryption ABB\nGUID-SEC-DATA-ENC-2.5.03]
        DLP[DLP ABB\nGUID-SEC-DATA-DLP-2.5.05]
        MASK[Masking ABB\nGUID-SEC-DATA-MASK-2.5.06]
    end

    subgraph Destinations["Delivery Contexts"]
        PROD[Production Systems\nFull data, encrypted]
        NONPROD[Non-Production\nMasked or synthetic data]
        ANALYTICS[Analytics / Reporting\nDynamic masking or aggregated]
        EGRESS[External Egress\nDLP-evaluated and policy-approved]
    end

    SRC --> AUTO
    AUTO --> LABEL
    LABEL --> CAT
    LABEL --> ROUTE
    ROUTE -->|Restricted/Regulated| ENC
    ROUTE -->|Any tier - egress| DLP
    ROUTE -->|Non-production request| MASK
    ENC --> PROD
    MASK --> NONPROD
    MASK --> ANALYTICS
    DLP --> EGRESS
```

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#classification-schema-architecture]

### Classification Schema Architecture

The enterprise classification schema SHALL be structured in two dimensions:

**Sensitivity Tier (vertical axis)**:

| Tier | Definition | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Public | Authorized for unrestricted public access | Marketing materials, public documentation |
| Internal | Not for external distribution; no regulated data | Internal procedures, non-PHI operational data |
| Restricted | Significant harm from unauthorized disclosure | PHI, PII, financial records, contractual data |
| Highly Restricted | Severe harm from disclosure; limited need-to-know | Encryption root keys, security architecture designs |

**Regulatory Sub-Tier (horizontal overlay)**:

| Sub-Tier | Applies To |
|---|---|
| PHI | Health information subject to HIPAA — applies within Restricted tier |
| PII | Personally identifiable information — applies within Restricted tier |
| CUI | Controlled Unclassified Information — applies within Restricted or Highly Restricted tier |

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#channel-coverage-model]

### Channel Coverage Model

| Egress Channel | DLP Enforcement Approach | Coverage Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Email | Inline content inspection at mail gateway | SHALL — for all restricted and regulated data |
| Cloud storage upload | API-level interception or CASB inspection | SHALL — for all restricted and regulated data |
| Web upload / HTTP POST | Proxy or endpoint-based inspection | SHALL — for all restricted and regulated data |
| Collaboration platforms | Platform-native DLP integration | SHOULD — where platform APIs support it |
| Removable media | Endpoint agent enforcement | SHOULD — for managed endpoints |
| API responses | Response content inspection | SHOULD — for high-sensitivity APIs |
| Print | Endpoint agent enforcement | MAY — proportional to print volume of sensitive data |

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#dlp-policy-governance]

### DLP Policy Governance

DLP policy SHALL be governed as a security configuration artifact:
- Policy changes require architecture review for significant scope changes
- Policy updates require testing in a representative environment before production deployment
- Unauthorized policy changes trigger a security incident
- Policy effectiveness metrics (detection rate, false positive rate, coverage gaps) SHALL be reviewed regularly

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#masking-gate-pattern]

### Masking Gate Pattern

Non-production data pipelines SHALL include a masking gate that executes before sensitive data reaches the non-production environment:

1. **Classification check**: Verify the classification tier of the source data
2. **Masking rule selection**: Select masking transformation rules appropriate to the classification tier and data types
3. **Transform**: Apply masking transformations — format-preserving substitution for values requiring referential integrity
4. **Validation**: Verify that no sensitive values survived the transformation (spot-check or automated scanning)
5. **Deliver**: Deliver the masked dataset to the non-production environment
page_texts.12:
[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#dynamic-masking-for-analytics]

### Dynamic Masking for Analytics

Where analytics consumers require access to production data with masking applied at query time:
- Masking rules are applied by the data platform based on the querying user's role
- Results returned to restricted-role users contain masked field values
- Results returned to authorized roles contain actual values
- All queries are audited with the requester's identity and the masking rules applied

[strategy/guidance/security/Data/ref-arch/GUID-SEC-DATA-CLASS-GOV-RAD-3.5.04.md#token-scope-and-vault-governance]

### Token Scope and Vault Governance

The token vault (the store mapping tokens to original sensitive values) SHALL be governed as a restricted data store:
- Access to the token vault is restricted to systems authorized for detokenization
- Detokenization requests are audited with the requesting system identity
- Token format-preservation SHALL be assessed per integration — format-preserving tokens minimize downstream integration changes
- Token lifetime SHALL be defined — tokens for transient operations should not persist indefinitely
